Practical training-free framework suitable for dynamic MAS deployments; addresses real operational constraints (32K+ token trajectories, computational efficiency) not adequately handled by prior methods

Weak absolute performance undermining practical utility: Acc@0 reaches only 12.1% best case; Acc@5 at 48.3% is forgiving (±5 steps); no human performance baseline provided; claim of 'substantially narrowing gap to human-level' unsupported

Limited scope and missing validation: no real-world deployment or case studies; no latency/cost analysis despite 'near-zero overhead' claims; 3 billion tokens spent generating schemas contradicts training-free framing; no temporal dynamics discussion (schema degradation, regeneration frequency); no out-of-distribution analysis

Overclaimed contributions: 'first schema-guided detector' (but schemas are LLM summaries), 'training-free' (relies on extensive LLM calls and careful prompting), 'large-scale' dataset (2,000 trajectories is moderate), 'high-fidelity' (47.1% misclassification is marginal)

Missing critical ablations: no ablation removing schema expansion/distillation; clustering quality and K selection not studied; embedding model (BAAI-BPE-M3) not ablated; no analysis of factors making schemas 'good' vs. 'bad'; performance plateaus quickly (Figure 8) suggesting limited schema diversity

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical importance for reliable MAS deployment; empirical observation that 80%+ of failures share semantic similarity provides strong motivation for schema-based approach

Practical and elegant solution addressing real limitations of existing approaches; long-tailed error distribution insight is well-validated experimentally and enables efficient schema caching

High-quality dataset contribution (CORRECT-Error with 2,000+ trajectories); three-stage synthesis pipeline is thoughtful with rigorous human validation (47.1% synthetic misclassified as human, 94.4% inter-annotator consensus)

Training-free, lightweight framework enabling adaptation to dynamic MAS deployments without expensive retraining; subsecond inference overhead
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (LLM-based schema extraction, semantic similarity retrieval, in-context example usage) are straightforward applications of existing methods rather than novel ML techniques

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing techniques (standard LLM prompting for schema generation, cosine similarity retrieval, context-guided prompting) without substantial algorithmic innovation
